answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake linked to a single cipher keypair and a history of useful work. Peers only trust a signal from an identity once its stake is locked and its past attestations check out, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up a grove of fake agents: each clone needs its own stake, its own key, and time to earn trust. Creating thousands of fakes therefore costs thousands of stakes plus forfeiture risk, while honest agents pay only once.
